title: Teen dies, police officer injured after chase in Niagara Falls
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit is investigating after a man died and a police officer was injured after falling over a retaining wall and into the Niagara Gorge Tuesday evening.
Niagara Regional Police confirmed that the officer was chasing the man when they both went over the railing around 5:34 p.m. on Tuesday.
Police say firefighters, Niagara Parks police and Niagara regional police were involved in the rescue, and firefighters used rappelling equipment to reach the men in the gorge.
The officer, identified as Constable Jacob Smits, was the first person to be pulled out of the gorge and transported by air ambulance to Hamilton General Hospital and underwent emergency surgery.
The second individual, whom Global News has identified as 18-year old Ryan Dube, was pronounced dead after being pulled from the gorge.
Dube had lived on and off at a Boys and Girls Club residence in Niagara and was "well-liked" according to the organization's executive director.
"He was always very respectful and polite," JoAnne Turner said. "He'll be missed. It's such a tragedy."
Turner also said that Dube was on probation, but was looking for a job and hoped to eventually live on his own.
The incident occurred near River Rd. between Eastwood St. and Otter St.
The SIU is an arm's length agency that comes in when police are involved in a death, serious injury or allegation of sexual assault.
